paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me: you can bring the LORD your whole heart, the ugly parts too. Jeremiah doesn't clean it up. He says, "You have deceived me, O LORD," and later he curses the day he was born (Jeremiah 20:7, 14). It's all right there in the Word, and nobody gets thrown out of the bakery for it.

Look at how it moves, though. In the middle of the mess, Jeremiah says, "But the LORD is with me like a fearsome warrior," and then, "Sing to the LORD! Praise the LORD!" (Jeremiah 20:11, 13). Then the very next words are a curse on his birthday. I think that tells us faith isn't a straight line, friend. It can go from praise to pain in one breath, and the praise was still real.

So what do you do when obeying God costs you? Jeremiah says if he tries to hold the LORD's message in, it becomes "a fire burning in my heart" (Jeremiah 20:9). He can't walk away, and he doesn't hide how heavy it is. This part of his cry is heavy, and I think the LORD wants us to bring our heaviest days to Him, the same way Jeremiah did. Tell Him the truth, baker, because "to You I have committed my cause" (Jeremiah 20:12).
